note: Curated list of results from the research record; each finding is pinned to its source file by SHA-256 (tests/test_findings_provenance.py).

findings.finding: Re-measuring spacecraft crater rims from LROC images does not improve mass accuracy
findings.result: Mass error with speed and angle known: 0.126 dex with published diameters, 0.141 dex with re-measured diameters (n = 11)

findings.finding: Crater-diameter precision beyond 0.02 dex barely narrows the mass range
findings.result: 10 m crater, 90% mass range: 1.64 dex at 0.02 dex diameter error, 1.63 dex at 0.005 dex, 1.97 dex at 0.10 dex

findings.finding: The scaling-law scatter between independent domains is about 0.065 dex and cannot be reduced below the assumed 0.10 dex
findings.result: 9 domains (laboratory sands, Ryugu, 4 spacecraft families); between-domain SD 0.065 dex; held-out-domain log score 9.96 (learned) vs 10.26 (fixed 0.10); coverage 7/9

findings.finding: Automatic detection of new craters in LROC before/after preview images does not work
findings.result: 40 known new craters: AUROC 0.54 (classical baseline), 0.59 (gradient-orthogonal change), chance 0.50; the pre-set viability bar was 0.75

findings.finding: Elongation and shallowness identify secondary craters in the Kepler region
findings.result: 610 Kepler-region craters, spatially held-out folds: AUROC 0.944, accuracy 0.897 (depth/diameter alone 0.866); one region only

findings.finding: Setting the secondary-crater weight from morphometry corrects the mass estimate
findings.result: 120 craters: mass error 1.54 dex (primaries assumed) vs 0.66 dex (classifier weight); 90% coverage 45% vs 93%
findings.status: in-model only; superseded by the region test below

findings.finding: The secondary-crater classifier does not transfer to another region
findings.result: Copernicus secondary field (Singer et al. 2020), 6149 craters of 1-1.5 km: AUROC 0.39 [0.36, 0.42]; secondaries there are deeper than surrounding craters (d/D 0.112 vs 0.084), the opposite of Kepler

findings.evidence: Real labels and crater data; simulated impactors for the mass effect
findings.finding: Crater shape plus the surrounding crater population identifies secondaries in regions the model has not seen
findings.result: 1842 independently labelled craters, 6 held-out regions: AUROC 0.84 [0.82, 0.85], weakest region 0.82 (shape alone 0.72). In the model (160 cases, simulated impactors), mass error 1.30 dex (default) vs 0.94 (context) and 0.97 (shape only)
findings.status: classification established; mass gain comes from shape, not context; label circularity unresolved; not in the engine

findings.finding: Removing classifier-predicted secondaries does not bring crater-count ages closer to radiometric sample ages
findings.result: 7 sample-return count areas, mean |log age ratio|: 0.041 with no removal, 0.063 (shape), 0.043 (shape + context), 0.039 (catalogue flag)

findings.evidence: Real (crater diameters, flash photometry); eta, speeds assumption-dependent
findings.finding: The flash-to-crater chain predicts held-out crater diameters when luminous efficiency comes from the other pairs
findings.result: 3 flash-crater pairs, leave-one-pair-out: 3/3 inside the 90% interval, mean |log D error| 0.115 dex (0.165 with the default eta prior)

findings.finding: The published luminous efficiency 6e-3 (Sheward et al. 2025) is driven by two craters below 5 m and by the choice of scaling law
findings.result: Reconstruction of their procedure with their plotted Holsapple law: eta 2.2e-03 with all six craters, 5.6e-04 without the two sub-5 m craters, 6.4e-04 with the three in-domain pairs
findings.status: established as far as the paper allows; exact statistic unresolved

findings.evidence: Real (flash rate, bolide flux, LROC new craters); no flash-crater pair used
findings.finding: Population rates imply a luminous efficiency about ten times higher than the three flash-crater pairs
findings.result: Flash rate vs bolide flux and vs LROC crater production: eta 6.1e-03 (90% 1.5e-03 to 2.5e-02). Predicting the three pairs with it: 1/3 inside the 90% interval, mean log D error -0.33 dex (pairs leave-one-out: 3/3, -0.00)
findings.status: unresolved tension; default eta range unchanged

findings.finding: A flat log-mass prior overestimates natural-impactor masses; each population now has its own mass prior
findings.result: 120 synthetic natural craters drawn from the Brown et al. 2002 size distribution: mass bias +0.48 dex and 90% coverage 0.75 with the former flat prior, -0.003 dex and 0.91 with the population prior (b = 0.90); spacecraft keep the flat prior (designed masses)
findings.status: adopted as the default (pre-registered); real natural masses cannot be checked
